findings.where: First screen, the contact row: the filled blue 'Write to me' button and the underlined address beside it (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The page's one personal action does nothing. 'Write to me' looks like a filled primary button but is static, and the underlined address next to it looks like a link but is also static. The only working mailto is the footer address, far down the page.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who clicks 'Write to me' or the address to email Mark gets no response. The page's main job, getting in touch with Mark, fails on the first screen.

findings.where: First screen, the three margin notes (Istanbul 2025, Melbourne 2026, São Paulo 2024 with their talk titles); also the blue specimen labels down the left margin (Palette, Type, Texture, Article page, Motion, Tile notes)
findings.fault: The notes are set in the house blue, which the palette names as the link colour, and they read as talk titles a visitor can open. They are all static, so nothing happens on a click. The brief asks for blue margin notes, so this clash with the link colour goes to the founder.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader who wants to check Mark's talks clicks a title and gets nothing. They lose the evidence they came for and may take the site for broken.

findings.where: First screen, the 'Book a consultation' button beside 'Write to me'
findings.fault: A second filled blue button, the same weight as 'Write to me', gives two primary actions. It also offers a booking that this brochure site doesn't provide: it only jumps to #consult, and no such section appears on the page.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because the brief asks for one direct, personal way to reach Mark, and a 'book a consultation' line sounds like a firm's sales funnel. A visitor, who has to choose between two equal buttons and then finds no booking.

findings.where: First screen, the ground behind the hero (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The hero sits on a pale lavender-to-pink gradient, not on the warm paper the tile's own palette names ('three colours, no accent'). The violet hue is in neither house colour, and the grey photo is no longer graded to the ground as the texture note claims.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for one soft warm ground with blue and grey as the only ink. A lilac gradient reads as a generic template look, not a legal journal.

findings.where: First screen, the first-person paragraph set in tracked bold capitals ('I ADVISE MULTILATERAL DEVELOPMENT BANKS…'), four lines on desktop and eight on phone
findings.fault: The paragraph that says who Mark is and whom he serves is set in spaced-out capitals. That makes it slow to read, and it shouts over both the serif body and the headline's calm voice.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor reading the key sentence of the 5-second test, and the founder, who asked for refined and serious type, not tracked caps.

findings.where: Phone, the contact row at the end of the hero
findings.fault: The address is wedged between the two buttons with almost no space around it, and 'Book a consultation' is indented from the left edge that the other items share. The group looks broken.
findings.who_objects: A phone visitor looking for how to reach Mark, who sees a cramped, misaligned cluster at the one point of action.

findings.where: First screen and the page as a whole: proof of Mark's work
findings.fault: The page has no third-party proof: no named client, testimonial or link out to a talk or publication hosted by a named body. The only hint, the static margin notes, can't be followed.
findings.who_objects: A development-agency reader who must check standing before shortlisting an individual adviser.

findings.where: Article specimen, the 'Download' button on the PDF row, against the hero's buttons
findings.fault: Buttons get two unrelated shapes: an outlined capsule here, square-cornered filled rectangles in the hero.
findings.who_objects: A careful reader and the founder, because like actions should look alike across a page Angélique will extend.

findings.where: Article specimen, the photo caption; compared with the hero caption
findings.fault: The article caption runs an italic serif line straight into a sans placeholder note in the same paragraph. The hero caption sets the same two parts on separate lines, so like captions are treated differently.
findings.who_objects: The founder, judging whether the type system holds when Angélique adds an image and caption.

findings.fault: The curve sits top left while the photo and timing table drop far down on the right, leaving a large dead area under the curve. The section reads as two parts that don't belong together.
findings.who_objects: The founder, reviewing the specimen, for whom the parts look scattered rather than set.

findings.where: Header navigation (Profile, Articles and Presentations, Blog)
findings.fault: The nav has no 'Contact' item, so the route to Mark depends on finding the hero buttons or the footer.
findings.who_objects: A returning visitor who scans the nav for how to reach Mark.
